analysis:
This batch has two documentation-only changes: the new changelog fragment changelog.d/startup-shape-warmup.md and an added paragraph at docs/architecture/hardware-support.md around head lines 534-541. No executable code, protocol fields, keys, attestation paths or authorization logic are modified.

The documented behavior is a startup shape warmup. It runs after model load and any self-test, and before provider registration and the local listener open. It uses the existing calibration session, idle gate and foreground lease. It stays within the existing KV and service budgets and publishes no observations or work totals. Requests preempt it, and the proactive MLX pool sweep waits while a session runs, though on-pressure reclaims still run.

Security-relevant observations, none of them findings on this evidence:
- The warmup uses synthetic probes, so I see no new exposure of consumer prompts (A-001) and no key material involved (A-003).
- The warmup runs before registration, so it delays registration by up to 20 s per model. Documentation states it is bounded and opt-out via DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP=0. This is a minor availability trade-off, not a regression.
- It does not publish observations or work totals, so it should not affect capacity or serving evidence reported to the coordinator. This depends on the unseen implementation.
- Shape warmup may fill the compiled-kernel cache. This is not a prefix-cache (T-041) change, and no cross-tenant state is described.

The implementation (Swift code) is not in this batch. Integration should confirm that the warmup does not use real consumer data, does not bypass the foreground lease or memory admission, and does not leak into prefix-cache donation (T-041) or the TTFT timing oracle. This batch gives no evidence of any of those, so no threat-model update is required from it.
